雲龍 · ASCII Dragons

A spatial Canvas character-rendering study inspired by:
https://github.com/stackedlol/ascii-sharks
Source inspected: a0074c16a106f0abc665fe9712ca445f8f98ad8e (2026-10-28)

The dragon rig, cloud module, character renderer, and interface were implemented
for this study. No shark simulation, meshes, images or source files are shipped.
The conceptual starting points are a Canvas character grid, a segmented spine,
turning and a trailing motion field. The moving spine follows the actual flight history of each head.
The flight skeleton and local anatomy frames have XYZ coordinates and are
perspective-projected into Canvas characters. There is no arbitrary-view
camera or fully modelled art mesh.

Visual reference (not distributed as an image asset):
National Palace Museum, Divine Dragon in Rain (attributed to Chen Rong).
https://theme.npm.edu.tw/MythicalCreatures115/page-3
Angular returning-cloud decoration is newly drawn, not an archaeological
reconstruction of a particular Sanxingdui object.
